purpose: The use-case directory band of a solution page: a left-aligned section title over a divider grid of linked topics, one per use case, each an icon, a heading and a sentence that link to the page that explains it — or, when the items carry no `href`, a plain grid of the same topics with nothing to follow. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'use-case-links', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — so its whole API is the props below, and it composes `section-module`, `section-title`, `frame-box`, `card-grid` and `topic` rather than owning anatomy of its own.
useWhen: When every use case has its own page and the band's job is to route the reader there.
For three or six use cases of equal weight, in a three-column grid.
For a link-less use-case grid under a left-aligned title (the KV Store page's "Use cases"): leave out every `href`.
avoidWhen: When the use cases carry no link and the band leads with one call to action → use `use-cases`.
related: use-cases` — the sibling band with a title cell and one action instead of a link per case.
topic` — the linked icon-heading-sentence cell each use case is rendered with.
bestPractices: Keep the count a multiple of three so the divider grid closes cleanly.
Link every item or none: an item without `href` renders as a plain topic (no link, no arrow), and a band that mixes both reads as broken.
Keep `description` to one sentence; the row height follows the longest cell.
